note: PIK3CA-mutant cell panels and xenografts carried alpelisib, taselisib and inavolisib to positive phase 3s in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- disease, the ER-feedback xenograft set the fulvestrant combination, and rodent and dog glucose intolerance predicted the hyperglycaemia that limited every member.

engagement.model: PIK3CA-mutant cell-line panel (CCLE) and PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer xenografts

Alpelisib's phase 1 (Juric 2018) abstract reports MTD and responses but no tumour PD; the class's hyperglycaemia is PI3Kα pharmacology in dosed humans but is the toxicology track's readout, scored there.

Patient samples came from patients already on BYL719 trials, so the confirmation was prospective to the model, not a retrodiction of a trial result.

dose.model: PIK3CA-mutant cell-line panel (CCLE) and PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer xenografts
dose.note: Mice were dosed to efficacy with tolerability stated, but no human exposure target was public before the phase 1.

dose.quote: The compound selectivity combined with excellent drug-like properties translates to dose- and time-dependent inhibition of PI3Kα signaling in vivo, resulting in robust therapeutic efficacy and tolerability in PIK3CA-dependent tumors.
dose.judgement: Opening entry; the tolerability statement is the margin decision 16 scores later.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; no exposure-level model-versus-patient comparison was read, so magnitude is null. Juric 2018 (doi 10.1200/JCO.2017.72.7107) gives the 400 mg MTD with hyperglycaemia as the DLT.
dose.model: PIK3CA-mutant cell-line panel (CCLE) and PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer xenografts
dose.note: Alpelisib 300 mg/day (phase 1 MTD 400 mg) was deliverable and beat placebo on PFS; hyperglycaemia at that dose was the predicted on-target effect.
dose.quote: we compared alpelisib (at a dose of 300 mg per day) plus fulvestrant (at a dose of 500 mg every 28 days and once on day 15) with placebo plus fulvestrant
dose.reason: Effective dose reached; stated tolerability held
dose.judgement: Rule row 'reached, drug worked'. Fritsch 2014 stated the efficacious mouse exposure was tolerated (margin_stated), and the harm at the human effective dose, hyperglycaemia, was the one the sponsor's mouse glucose-tolerance study had predicted, so the margin was not misplaced and decision 16's toxicity block does not apply. Class-consistent: taselisib 4 mg (DLTs at 12-16 mg) met SANDPIPER's primary endpoint and inavolisib 9 mg met INAVO120's; taselisib's 36.5% dose reductions and 16.8% discontinuations are a safety matter, not a dose failure, because the endpoint was met at that dose.

dose.model: ER+ PIK3CA-mutant breast lines, xenografts and PDX under PI3Kα inhibition (ER-feedback model)
dose.note: Xenograft and PDX dosing of BYL719 with fulvestrant; no exposure target or tolerability margin in the abstract.
dose.quote: Fulvestrant markedly sensitized ER-positive tumors to PI3Kα inhibition, resulting in major tumor regressions in vivo.
dose.judgement: The combination prediction went into SOLAR-1 at alpelisib's monotherapy-derived dose; nothing in this model set an exposure target, so dose stays untested on this track.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the xenograft line is not named in the abstract. model_filed null: taselisib has no NDA.
efficacy.model: PIK3CA-mutant cell-line panel (CCLE) and PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer xenografts
efficacy.note: Taselisib suppressed xenograft growth at low doses; class-level prediction that a PI3Kα-selective inhibitor controls PI3K-driven tumours.
efficacy.short: Xenograft growth suppressed at low dose
efficacy.quote: By lowering the intrinsic clearance, we derived a set of imidazobenzoxazepin compounds that showed improved unbound drug exposure and effectively suppressed growth of tumors in a mouse xenograft model at low drug dose levels.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the class's first xenograft use; Fritsch 2014 adds the patient-level stratification on the same track.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the FDA review (NDA 212526) gives the numbers: 65% of PIK3CA-mutant vs 23% of wild-type lines sensitive (IC50 < 3 µM) across 474 lines, and calls the selectivity claim insufficiently supported.
efficacy.model: PIK3CA-mutant cell-line panel (CCLE) and PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer xenografts
efficacy.note: CCLE screen: PIK3CA mutation the foremost predictor of alpelisib sensitivity, PTEN mutation a negative one; the stratification was written into the trials.
efficacy.short: PIK3CA mutation predicts sensitivity in cell panel
efficacy.quote: we also describe the application of the Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia as a preclinical platform to refine the patient stratification strategy for NVP-BYL719 and found that PIK3CA mutation was the foremost positive predictor of sensitivity
efficacy.judgement: Same track, same status, so strengthens: this is the patient-level prediction the 2019 entry scores.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: model: 65% of PIK3CA-mutant vs 23% of wild-type lines sensitive (IC50 < 3 µM); patients: PFS HR 0.65 in the mutant cohort vs 0.85 in the non-mutant cohort
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (NEJM). SANDPIPER's registry results (2019-01-25), SOLAR-1's NEJM paper (May 2019) and SOLAR-1's registry results (2019-08-13) all fall in 2019; the tier 1 record sets the status.
efficacy.model: PIK3CA-mutant cell-line panel (CCLE) and PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer xenografts
efficacy.note: SOLAR-1 primary endpoint met in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort (PFS 11.0 vs 5.7 months, HR 0.65); the non-mutant cohort missed its proof-of-concept criterion (HR 0.85).
efficacy.quote: progression-free survival at a median follow-up of 20 months was 11.0 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 7.5 to 14.5) in the alpelisib-fulvestrant group, as compared with 5.7 months (95% CI, 3.7 to 7.4) in the placebo-fulvestrant group

patient_trials.quote: Confirmed response rate was 36% for PIK3CA-mutant tumor patients with measurable disease [5/14: 4 breast cancer (3 patients at 12 mg); 1 non-small cell lung cancer], where responses started at 3 mg, and 0% in patients with tumors without known PIK3CA hotspot mutations (0/15).
those lesions that became refractory to BYL719 had additional and different PTEN genetic alterations, resulting in the loss of PTEN expression.

INV-PFS was significantly improved in the taselisib {7.4 months [95% confidence interval (CI), 7.26-9.07]} versus placebo arm (5.4 months [95% CI, 3.68-7.29]) (stratified hazard ratio [HR] 0.70; 95% CI, 0.56-0.89; P = 0.0037)

The median progression-free survival was 15.0 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 11.3 to 20.5) in the inavolisib group and 7.3 months (95% CI, 5.6 to 9.3) in the placebo group (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.59; P<0.001).

efficacy.judgement: Patient-level prediction scored on the primary endpoint: benefit in the PIK3CA-mutant cohort and none meeting the proof-of-concept bar in the non-mutant cohort is the stratification Fritsch 2014 proposed. Magnitude is direction_only because a cell-panel sensitivity fraction has no PFS equivalent. Every member matched: taselisib's SANDPIPER met its primary endpoint (HR 0.70) though Roche dropped it for benefit-risk, so it is not a neg (its model data were not below the class bar and the trial did not fail); inavolisib's INAVO120 (HR 0.43) is the strongest. The panel's PTEN-loss negative prediction was borne out in Juric 2015's resistant metastases (a stated comparison, but a resistance case series rather than a trial endpoint, so under patient_trials). SOLAR-1's final overall survival (2021, not significant) was not read with a tool call and is not scored.

efficacy.model: ER+ PIK3CA-mutant breast lines, xenografts and PDX under PI3Kα inhibition (ER-feedback model)
efficacy.note: Prediction: fulvestrant sensitises ER+ PIK3CA-mutant tumours to PI3Kα inhibition, so combined PI3K and ER inhibition is the way to treat them.
efficacy.short: Fulvestrant plus PI3Kα inhibitor regresses xenografts
efficacy.quote: Fulvestrant markedly sensitized ER-positive tumors to PI3Kα inhibition, resulting in major tumor regressions in vivo.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry; the FDA review of NDA 212526 cites this paper as the basis for the fulvestrant combination.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: model: major regressions with fulvestrant plus BYL719 versus growth delay with either alone; patients: PFS HR 0.65 versus fulvestrant alone
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The model compared the combination with each single agent; SOLAR-1 compared it with fulvestrant only, and alpelisib monotherapy PFS (5.5 months, Juric 2018 phase 1) is a cross-trial figure.
efficacy.model: ER+ PIK3CA-mutant breast lines, xenografts and PDX under PI3Kα inhibition (ER-feedback model)
efficacy.note: SOLAR-1 tested the model's combination: alpelisib plus fulvestrant beat fulvestrant alone on PFS in PIK3CA-mutant disease.
efficacy.quote: progression-free survival at a median follow-up of 20 months was 11.0 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 7.5 to 14.5) in the alpelisib-fulvestrant group, as compared with 5.7 months (95% CI, 3.7 to 7.4) in the placebo-fulvestrant group

patient_trials.quote: An objective response occurred in 58.4% of the patients in the inavolisib group and in 25.0% of those in the placebo group.

efficacy.judgement: The model predicted that ER blockade plus PI3Kα inhibition beats either alone; the trial that followed tested the combination against fulvestrant and met its primary endpoint, so same in direction. The half of the prediction about PI3Kα monotherapy being limited by ER feedback was never randomised against the combination, hence medium confidence. INAVO120 (fulvestrant plus palbociclib backbone) strengthens without changing status.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; cited as Song et al. 2022 in the FDA review of NDA 219249.
efficacy.model: HER2-dependent mutant-p110α degradation model (HCC1954 PIK3CA H1047R cells and xenografts) for inavolisib and taselisib
efficacy.note: Predicts degraders (inavolisib, taselisib) hold pathway suppression longer than non-degrading PI3Kα inhibitors and have a better therapeutic index; no head-to-head trial exists.
efficacy.quote: Both are more effective than other PI3K inhibitors at maintaining prolonged pathway suppression.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track because the prediction differs from Track A's: not 'PI3Kα inhibition works in PIK3CA-mutant tumours' but 'mutant-selective degradation gives a wider window than alpelisib'. INAVO120 was placebo-controlled on a different backbone and SANDPIPER's benefit-risk was worse than SOLAR-1's, so the claim is neither confirmed nor refuted; a cross-trial reading would go against it for taselisib.

efficacy.model: Patient-derived xenograft of the index patient's PTEN-null, BYL719-refractory lung metastasis, with PTEN-knockdown isogenic PIK3CA-mutant cell lines
efficacy.note: PDX from the BYL719-refractory PTEN-null lesion was resistant to BYL719 in mice, reproducing the index patient's progression; sensitive to pan-PI3K and alpha+beta blockade.

efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the lesion was already clinically refractory when the PDX was made, so reproducing resistance is retro, not same (decision 10). Comparison stated in the paper. Single patient, magnitude direction only; endpoint_role null because the patient side is one patient's RECIST progression, not a trial endpoint.

efficacy.population: PIK3CA-mutant HR+ metastatic breast cancer with acquired PTEN loss on alpelisib

Razavi cites the preclinical PTEN work ('consistent with preclinical studies') rather than restating the PDX result, so paired (comparison_stated false), model_src Juric 2015. Direction only: the model predicted resistance, not a rate.
efficacy.reason: PTEN loss found in 25% of resistant patients
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PDX/knockdown resistance to BYL719 vs PTEN loss-of-function alterations in 8/32 patients with resistance to alpelisib + AI

efficacy.note: Isogenic MCF10A clones with cis double PIK3CA mutations were more sensitive to alpelisib and GDC-0077 (IC50, Emax, AUC) than single-hotspot clones.

efficacy.note: SANDPIPER ctDNA: multiple-PIK3CA-mutant ORR 30.2% vs 8.7% on taselisib vs placebo (P=0.0493); single-mutant 18.1% vs 10.0% (n.s.), as the cells predicted.

Not cited in the alpelisib or inavolisib FDA reviews (grep Vasan, double mutation), so model_filed false.

Comparison stated in the paper. endpoint_role null because the readout is an exploratory subgroup of a secondary endpoint; magnitude direction only (cell IC50 shifts vs ORR).
efficacy.reason: Multiple-mutant ORR 30% vs single 18% on taselisib
efficacy.magnitude_basis: cell IC50/Emax/AUC shift (double vs single mutant) vs ORR on taselisib + fulvestrant: multiple-mutant 30.2% vs single-mutant 18.1% (SANDPIPER, NCT02340221)

patient_trials.quote: Patients with double–PIK3CA-mutant tumors had a longer median PFS than did patients with single-mutant tumors or wild-type (WT) tumors, but this was not statistically significant because of the small number of cases

efficacy.model: Isogenic MCF7 ESR1 Y537S knock-in versus wild-type xenografts on alpelisib plus oestrogen deprivation
efficacy.note: ESR1 Y537S xenografts progressed faster than wild-type on alpelisib plus oestrogen deprivation, matching ESR1-mutation enrichment and VAF expansion in patients progressing on alpelisib plus AI.

efficacy.quote: Treatment of xenograft tumors from these models revealed that, compared to ESR1 WT tumors, ESR1 mutant-expressing tumors more rapidly progressed on the combination of alpelisib and estrogen deprivation (Fig. 4e).

efficacy.judgement: Retro (decision 10): built to explain a known patient result and reproduced it, so retro and counted apart from same. Comparison stated in the paper ('perhaps explaining mutation enrichment among pre-treatment ctDNA samples of patients who did not benefit'). Direction only; endpoint_role null (exploratory ctDNA association, primary objective was safety).
efficacy.reason: ESR1-mutant xenografts progress faster, as patients did

efficacy.population: PIK3CA-mutant HR+ metastatic breast cancer on alpelisib + aromatase inhibitor, ESR1-mutant

safety.model: PIK3CA-mutant cell-line panel (CCLE) and PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer xenografts

safety.quote: The compound selectivity combined with excellent drug-like properties translates to dose- and time-dependent inhibition of PI3Kα signaling in vivo, resulting in robust therapeutic efficacy and tolerability in PIK3CA-dependent tumors.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; no body-weight or glucose data read.
safety.model: ER+ PIK3CA-mutant breast lines, xenografts and PDX under PI3Kα inhibition (ER-feedback model)
safety.note: Abstract silent on tolerability of BYL719 with fulvestrant in mice; the class harm is scored on the toxicology track.
safety.quote: Fulvestrant markedly sensitized ER-positive tumors to PI3Kα inhibition, resulting in major tumor regressions in vivo.
safety.judgement: Opening entry; not scored as silence contradicted because the sponsor's own animals predicted the hyperglycaemia (toxicology track).

safety.magnitude_basis: animal hyperglycaemia and insulin insensitivity present versus 36.6% grade 3-4 hyperglycaemia in SOLAR-1 (0.7% placebo)
safety.confidence_note: FDA multidisciplinary review read by grep (nonclinical secondary pharmacology, mouse insulin/glucose tolerance study, AESI section, which says the AESIs were chosen partly on nonclinical observations). No untested opener: the toxicology program predates the 2010 phase 1 but has no public source before this review.
safety.model: Sponsor toxicology and secondary pharmacology (mouse insulin/glucose tolerance, rat and dog repeat-dose studies)
safety.note: Animals showed hyperglycaemia and insulin insensitivity (and skin findings in pigmented rats); SOLAR-1 grade 3-4 hyperglycaemia 36.6% vs 0.7%, rash 9.9%.

safety.quote: Alpelisib was also shown to cause hyperglycemia and insulin insensitivity in animals, in secondary pharmacology studies.
safety.judgement: Predicted harm appeared: hyperglycaemia was the phase 1 DLT (Juric 2018) and SOLAR-1's leading grade 3-4 event, so same with a stated comparison in a tier 2 document.

safety.magnitude_basis: rat/dog hyperglycaemia at >=0.1x and >=0.8x the human AUC versus 60% any-grade, 5.6% grade 3-4 hyperglycaemia in INAVO120
safety.confidence_note: FDA multidisciplinary review, nonclinical executive summary, which places the animal and the 60% patient incidence in one paragraph.
safety.model: Sponsor toxicology and secondary pharmacology (mouse insulin/glucose tolerance, rat and dog repeat-dose studies)
safety.note: Rats and dogs showed reversible hyperglycaemia from 0.1x/0.8x the human AUC and lens changes; patients: 60% hyperglycaemia, grade 1-2 ocular events.
safety.short: Rat and dog hyperglycaemia and eye findings recurred
safety.quote: Hyperglycemia was observed in both rats and dogs at ≥ 1 mg/kg/day (≥ 0.1 times the human exposure at the recommended dose of 9 mg/day based on AUC)
safety.judgement: Predicted harm appeared in every member (alpelisib DLT, taselisib dose-dependent, inavolisib 60%), so same, not other. Not scored: taselisib's colitis/diarrhoea (SANDPIPER SAEs 32%) and inavolisib's stomatitis, because taselisib has no nonclinical record (no NDA) and the inavolisib review's GI and oral findings were not read; if the animals were silent on a harm they could show, this track would go contra. Alpelisib's severe cutaneous reactions sit beside skin findings in pigmented rats in the review, read only at grep level.
